title: Laredo trucking company owner indicted over alleged B-1 visa driver scheme
excerpt: The owner of a Laredo trucking company has been indicted on allegations he hired 57 drivers on B-1 visas to haul freight inside the United States, paying them far less per mile than authorized drivers and saving nearly $300,000. He faces up to 10 years in prison if convicted.
content:
The owner of a Laredo trucking company has been indicted on allegations that he hired 57 drivers on B-1 visas to haul freight inside the United States, according to KGNS.

Armando Martinez Varela, 56, owns VMS Transport in Laredo. Federal prosecutors allege he used the B-1 visa drivers for domestic hauls, according to the Laredo Morning Times. B-1 visas allow some international trucking work, but they do not authorize drivers to haul freight within the United States, KGNS reported.

Prosecutors allege Varela paid the drivers between 25 and 50 cents per mile, while authorized drivers would have received 70 cents per mile, according to KGNS. The difference saved the company nearly $300,000, the station reported.

If convicted, Varela faces up to 10 years in prison, according to KGNS.

The indictment was reported on Wednesday, Nov. 11. The case is the latest federal enforcement action tied to Laredo's trucking industry, a sector that sits at the center of cross-border freight moving through Webb County.

Sources: KGNS, Nov. 11, 2026; Laredo Morning Times, Nov. 11, 2026.
